A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRG research work. All 14 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original PRG classification, corruption-robustness, transfer-learning and ablation results, including numerical tables and reverse-generation visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original PRG experiments and adds results for pretraining controls, loss weighting, inference efficiency and dual-task transfer.

M1.justification: v2 Eq. (3) adds a beta-weighted flow-matching loss to the cross-entropy fine-tuning objective in v1 Eq. (13). This is a bounded objective change within the retained reversible ODE and two-layer classifier framework. The PDFs do not establish that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix C.5 adds a stated dual-task transfer scenario using different positions of one SiT trajectory for CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet; v1 reports separate downstream transfers. The underlying datasets, corruption domains and Swiss-roll examples remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 newly include PRG-GVP-onlyPretrain as an internal comparator, and v2 Table 8 explicitly compares against training without pretraining. External comparator membership in the corresponding classification, corruption and standard transfer tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experimental protocols include a 600-epoch nonpretrained control, a beta sweep over 1, 10 and 100, and a 30-step dual-task trajectory with features extracted at steps 10 and 20. The existing dataset-specific training configuration tables are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends mechanism validation through a long-trained nonpretrained control across three datasets and sensitivity analysis of the newly introduced joint-objective weight. It also adds CIFAR-10 solver sensitivity and dual-task transfer analysis. Earlier freezing, corruption, scaling, timestep and visualization analyses remain; the Tiny-ImageNet solver study is relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.3.1 newly documents Gaussian-probe Hutchinson trace estimation for the log-density diagnostic, adding a statistical estimation procedure absent from v1's description. This does not establish additional runs. Neither version supplies seed counts or explains the uncertainty bands in Figure 3.

E6.justification: Headline classification, corruption and standard transfer scores remain unchanged, but substantial result blocks are added: pretrain-only accuracies of 54.10%, 15.34% and 20.18%, nonpretrained controls, beta and solver results, inference timings, and dual-task accuracies of 96.9% and 70.2%. Figure 3's diagnostic curves also change. The dual-task scores use different conditions from the retained Table 7 transfer results.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit low-dimensional-manifold assumption and a topology-preservation argument in Appendix A, plus mathematical reasoning about changing latent entropy and the mutual-information diagnostic in Section 4.3.1. The original KL/likelihood derivation is retained; no new theorem or completed proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central model-agnostic reversal contribution and approximately 78% ImageNet claim remain. However, v2's introduction replaces the claimed supervised-and-unsupervised classification scope with classification, OOD detection and successful community text-to-image transfer. Its abstract also specifies the existing 64 × 64 ImageNet resolution.

C2.justification: The new Appendix A substantially expands mechanism explanations through manifold lifting, preserved topology, pretrained initialization and distinctions between training-depth benefits and inference-depth saturation. Section 4.3.1 adds qualifications concerning latent entropy when interpreting the diagnostic. These extend v1's shorter information-preservation and feature-pruning discussion; the concluding limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents optimal-transport coupling, adjoint/Hutchinson diagnostic computation, dual-task trajectory settings and inference timings. Existing hardware and hyperparameter tables remain. Appendix B.2 changes the stated experiment duration from '2 hours to 3 days' to 'several hours' despite retaining the same per-epoch timing values.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Bao's diffusion ViT work, Hutchinson's trace estimator and Murphy's textbook, while removing citations including the corruption benchmark, label-smoothing paper and Peebles–Xie diffusion Transformers. Positioning against architecture-dependent feature extraction is expanded, but the central relationship to generative classifiers and denoising representation learning remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: standalone preliminaries are condensed into the method framework, related work moves earlier, and the framework precedes its mechanism explanation. It adds a baseline subsection and reorganizes the appendices around explanations, implementation, ablations and visualizations. Introduction and method passages are also extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds compact tables for pretraining controls, beta sensitivity, inference timing and CIFAR-10 solvers, and adds rows to Tables 3–5. Figure 3 is redrawn with revised curves and scaling. Existing solver tables and appendix visualizations are relocated and recaptioned; the underlying visual examples and two-column design are retained.

improvement.justification: New controls, inference timings and computation details improve evidential coverage and documentation. However, Eq. (3) places beta in fine-tuning while Section 4.5.2 describes it as pretraining, and new text-to-image/OOD-detection claims exceed the class-conditional SiT transfer and corruption-classification evaluations described. The linkage between the revised objective and retained results is also unclear. These benefits and new consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
